items.title: Maximális súlyosságú hibát javított a GitLab A GitLab maximális súlyosságú távoli kódfuttatási hibát javított a CI/CD rendszerében. A hiba lehetővé tette, hogy egy be nem jelentkezett támadó egy spec…
items.summary: GitLab patched a maximum-severity remote code execution flaw in its CI/CD component that an unauthenticated attacker could exploit via a crafted configuration.

items.title: 2026-016: Critical Vulnerability in GitLab CE and EE
items.summary: CERT-EU advisory: GitLab CE/EE 19.4.2, 19.3.4 and 19.2.8 fix 24 issues including a critical unauthenticated RCE; prioritise internet-facing self-managed instances.

items.title: 2026-014: Critical Vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway
items.summary: CERT-EU flags 8 Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway vulnerabilities, including two critical unauthenticated RCEs confirmed exploited in the wild; patch and run compromise assessments.

items.title: Microsoft Patches Record 1,413 Flaws, Including Exploited Windows Shell Bug
items.summary: Microsoft's October Patch Tuesday fixed a record 1,413 flaws (1,102 in Windows), including an actively exploited Windows Shell bug; over 670 are privilege escalation issues.

items.title: Microsoft Patches More Than 1,400 Security Flaws
items.summary: Krebs reports Microsoft shipped fixes for more than 1,400 vulnerabilities, dwarfing September's record of nearly 1,000 and roughly ten times the historical monthly volume.

items.title: Patch Tuesday - October 2026
items.summary: Rapid7's analysis of October Patch Tuesday: 1,413 Microsoft vulnerabilities, one exploited in the wild (Windows Shell security feature bypass) and two publicly disclosed.

items.title: Ivanti Connect Secure zero-day exploited in the wild (CVE-2026-104935)
items.summary: Ivanti Connect Secure zero-day CVE-2026-104935 (CVSS 8.6) allows unauthenticated remote command execution via authentication bypass; exploited in the wild and added to CISA KEV.

items.title: CISA Urges Patching Newly Exploited Vulnerability in Ivanti Connect Secure
items.summary: CISA urges immediate patching of Ivanti Connect Secure CVE-2026-104935, exploited for credential theft and data exfiltration and added to the KEV catalog on 13 October.

items.title: CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
items.summary: CISA added two actively exploited vulnerabilities to KEV: a Microsoft Windows command injection (CVE-2026-96951) and the Ivanti Connect Secure authentication bypass (CVE-2026-104935).

items.title: CVE-2026-97229: Critical Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in GitLab
items.summary: Rapid7 details CVE-2026-97229, a CVSS 10.0 integer overflow in GitLab's CI/CD regex compiler enabling remote code execution via a crafted CI/CD configuration.

items.title: Gyenge jelszavak miatt szivárogtak ki milliók személyes adatai A dán központi népesség-nyilvántartás (CPR) elleni jelentős adatszivárgása jól példázza, hogy akár egyetlen gyenge jelszó és a partneri…
items.summary: Hungarian NKI reports a major breach of Denmark's central population register (CPR), attributed to weak passwords and supplier/partner access weaknesses, exposing millions of citizens' personal data.

items.title: MI ügynökökkel támadta az ukrán kritikus infrastruktúrát, egy konfigurációs hiba leplezte le Egy oroszul beszélő, pénzügyi motivációjú kiberbűnöző mesterséges intelligenciával támogatott eszközökkel…
items.summary: A Russian-speaking, financially motivated actor used AI agent-based tooling against Ukrainian critical infrastructure; a configuration error exposed the operation.

items.title: Europol urges early action to protect cryptocurrencies and sensitive data from quantum threats
items.summary: Europol urges organisations to act now on post-quantum readiness, stressing crypto-agility for protecting cryptocurrencies and sensitive data regardless of when quantum capabilities arrive.

items.title: Ransomware Gangs Embrace Physical Threats, Family Stalking?
items.summary: Dark Reading reports organisations claiming ransomware crews now threaten employees' families with stalking and physical violence, though such claims are difficult to verify.

items.title: Ransomware gets personal: 'We-know-where-you-are kind of stuff'
items.summary: A global survey finds 37% of ransomware attacks involve psychological or physical threats against staff, a shift beyond purely digital extortion.

items.title: Most companies count AI agents as insiders, and CISOs worry about their own liability
items.summary: A Trellix survey of 600 CISOs found 95% had an AI agent or autonomous system linked to an insider incident in the past year; 78% now treat AI agents and machine identities as insiders.

items.title: Ivanti misses opportunity to fix vulnerability before attackers got to work and made it a zero-day
items.summary: CyberScoop reports Ivanti partially identified the flaw internally in June but deemed it below the bar for an out-of-band fix, before attackers turned it into a zero-day.

items.title: DOJ charges 14 over a sprawling North Korean remote work scheme
items.summary: The US DOJ charged 14 people in Operation Lonestar Roundup over a North Korean remote-worker scheme that used stolen identities to funnel $3 million from 70 US employers to Pyongyang.

items.title: Anthropic warns self-replicating AI could spread to your smart devices
items.summary: Anthropic warns that small AI models could self-replicate across consumer IoT devices such as Android TV boxes and smart ovens, forming distributed botnets running AI workloads outside data centres.

items.title: Two arrested as DOJ takes down laptop farms responsible for $3 million in North Korean revenue
items.summary: US authorities dismantled laptop farms across more than 40 Texas residences, with two arrests, tied to North Korean remote-worker schemes generating $3 million.

items.title: Anthropic Finds Ingredients for Future AI Worms
items.summary: Anthropic research combining IoT and network testing suggests the building blocks for AI self-replication exist, and such worms would be challenging to shut down.

items.title: Russia remains 'aggressor number one,' UK's MI5 spy agency chief warns in threat update
items.summary: MI5 chief Ken McCallum calls Russia 'aggressor number one', noting an escalation of alleged Russian hybrid attacks across Europe as its military progress in Ukraine stalls.

items.title: In Frankreich wurden Kühlanlagen manipuliert – geht das auch bei uns?
items.summary: CERT.at examines the manipulation of refrigeration systems at French retail chains on 11/12 October that spoiled frozen goods, raising questions about exposed ICS components and similar risk elsewhere.

items.title: 9,6 millió dolláros bírságot kapott a Microsoft hirdetéstechnológiai cége a Grindr-adatok jogellenes megosztása miatt A norvég adatvédelmi hatóság (Datatilsynet) 92 millió norvég korona (mintegy 9,6…
items.summary: Norway's DPA fined a Microsoft advertising technology subsidiary NOK 92 million (~USD 9.6M) over unlawful sharing of Grindr user data.

items.title: Patching and preventing issues: What are the lessons you can learn?
items.summary: Interview with Qualys' Kunal Modasiya on why patching still fails: business pressure, revenue-critical systems and breaking patches, and why the exposure-to-weaponization gap matters more than raw speed.

items.title: Russian strikes hit key power plant in Kyiv, Zelensky says
items.summary: Russian ballistic missiles struck Kyiv's power plant infrastructure; Zelensky said there was no early warning from partners.

items.title: Saudi-born engineer for OpenAI arrested for planting listening bug
items.summary: OpenAI says a hidden recording device was found in one of its offices; a Saudi-born engineer has been arrested.

items.title: Russian missile hits Kyiv power plant with no early warning from allies, Zelensky says
items.summary: A Russian ballistic missile hit Kyiv's CHP-4 power plant; Zelensky criticised allies for lack of advance warning despite claims of an energy ceasefire.

items.title: OpenAI Employee Arrested for Allegedly Planting Hidden Recorder in Executive Conference Room
items.summary: An OpenAI employee was arrested and charged with planting a hidden recording device in an executive conference room to intercept oral communications.

items.title: An OpenAI Employee Allegedly Used a Chatbot to Help Plant a Recording Device at the Office
items.summary: Wired reports chatbot prompts allegedly show an OpenAI engineer using an AI assistant to help prepare the covert listening device found in an executive meeting room.

items.title: North Korea Phishes Ukrainians for War Intel
items.summary: Dark Reading reports North Korean actors are running simple reply-baiting phishing campaigns against Ukrainian targets to gather intelligence on the war.

items.title: OpenAI and Anthropic Tell British Lawmakers: Regulate Us
items.summary: OpenAI and Anthropic asked British lawmakers for regulation at a parliamentary session, while the UK intelligence chief warned AI could aid bioweapon development.

items.title: EU advances Ukraine accession as Hungary lifts veto, paving way for Zelenskyy-Magyar meeting
items.summary: EU governments opened two further accession clusters with Ukraine after Hungary lifted its veto following an agreement on ethnic Hungarian minority rights.

items.title: Tageszusammenfassung - 13.10.2026
items.summary: CERT.at daily report notes 31 newly disclosed MarkLogic Server flaws, five critical, two of which could let partially privileged accounts seize admin control; fixes in 11.3.7 and 12.1.0.

items.title: EDPB publishes statement on the data protection challenges of smart glasses
items.summary: The EDPB adopted a statement and report on smart glasses, flagging data protection risks around video recording, surveillance and evidence handling.

items.title: US state lawmakers highlight chatbot bills, AI's impact on mental health
items.summary: US state legislators are pushing chatbot-related bills, focusing on AI's effects on mental health.

items.title: Ukrainian drones strike more than 100km into Russian territory
items.summary: Ukrainian drones struck Russia's Saratov region more than 100km beyond the border, with one person reported killed.

items.title: Meshery: Open-source cloud-native manager for Kubernetes
items.summary: Overview of Meshery, an open-source CNCF-hosted tool for visually designing, validating and deploying Kubernetes infrastructure across clusters and clouds.

items.title: Ukrainian ex-officer goes on trial in Germany over Nord Stream blasts
items.summary: A former Ukrainian officer went on trial in Germany over the Nord Stream pipeline blasts; proceedings may run into February.

items.title: Kyiv hit by Russian ballistic missiles for second day with no warning
items.summary: Kyiv was hit by Russian ballistic missiles for a second consecutive day without advance warning.

items.title: Bank of America hit with $1.2bn fine for money laundering failings
items.summary: Bank of America was fined $1.2bn for anti-money-laundering failings tied to inadequate flagging of transactions linked to Chinese laundering networks.

items.title: How Europe can increase resilience to global shocks — live updates
items.summary: Live coverage from Politico's European Resilience Summit on strengthening Europe's resilience to global shocks.

items.title: Corruption could become harder to catch under new EU budget, watchdog warns
items.summary: The European Court of Auditors warns that greater spending flexibility in the new EU budget could make tracing corruption harder.

items.title: Employee Arrested After Listening Device Found in OpenAI Conference Room, FBI and the Company Say
items.summary: SecurityWeek: Saudi national Abdulrahman Alfozan was arrested and terminated by OpenAI after a listening device was found in a conference room, per the FBI and the company.

items.title: Redesigning source control at Anthropic
items.summary: Anthropic describes building a custom Git alternative after daily merged code changes rose from ~2,500 in May 2026 to over 30,000 by September, driven by AI coding agents.

items.title: Burnham pledges ‘rock-solid support’ for Ukraine as Zelenskyy makes UK trip
items.summary: The UK pledged continued support for Ukraine, with ministers asked to prepare further sanctions, military aid and fiscal packages during Zelenskyy's visit.

items.title: Violence in Paris as tens of thousands turn out for student protests across France
items.summary: Tens of thousands joined student protests across France; 11 police officers were hospitalised after clashes in Paris.

items.title: Europe’s leaders abandon the race for frontier AI
items.summary: Politico reports European leaders are shifting away from competing on frontier AI models toward adopting and applying AI.

items.title: From no cards to many: Europe warns Trump not to waste Ukraine’s leverage
items.summary: European officials urge the US not to squander Ukraine's leverage as Kyiv's strikes on Russian refineries complicate Washington's position.

items.title: Russian strike injures dozens at Rivne University as ballistic missiles hit Kyiv
items.summary: Russian strikes across Ukraine injured dozens at a university in Rivne and hit civilian infrastructure in Kyiv.

items.title: Quoting Geoffrey Huntley
items.summary: Commentary on enforcing coding-agent behaviour through pre-commit hooks that fail builds and inject corrective prompts rather than relying on agent instruction files.

items.title: Europe paid Russia $209bn for energy since 2022, far below Moscow’s $320bn claim
items.summary: The European Commission disputes Russian and US claims, saying Europe paid $209bn for Russian energy since 2022 rather than $320bn.

items.title: Vulnérabilité dans NetApp StorageGRID (13 octobre 2026)
items.summary: CERT-FR reports a vulnerability in NetApp StorageGRID that allows a remote attacker to cause a denial of service.
